recipes.name: Holly's Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough Dip

steps.text: Beat together cream cheese, butter, confectioners' sugar, brown sugar, and vanilla in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium-high speed until smooth and creamy.
Stir in chocolate chips until well combined.
Transfer cookie dough to a serving bowl. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Holly's Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough Dip
raw_recipe.description: Chocolate chip cookie dough dip is a new twist on dessert for any aged crowd. Dip graham crackers and vanilla wafer into this sweet chocolate treat.
raw_recipe.name: Holly's Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough Dip

review.reviewBody: Although this dessert dip does not taste like cookie dough that much (mostly because the cream cheese taste is very prevalent), it is still delicious and addicting! I added 2 extra tablespoons of brown sugar and an extra teaspoon of vanilla. I also added Heath toffee chips (for more texture) as I have seen in similar recipes. Oh, and I let this sit over night. At first, I served the dip with chocolate graham crackers, which were good, but then my husband had the fantastic idea to dip small pretzels in it. The salty/sweet combo was perfect! Next time, I may even add some crushed pretzels to the dip rather than the Heath chips. The salt of the pretzels really complimented the sugar in the dip! I will definitely make this dip again!

This recipe is good as written, but it does require a slight stretch of the imagination to taste a “cookie dough” flavor. After several attempts at tweaking, I’ve decided that I like it best using the mini semi- sweet chocolate chips and doubling the amount of brown sugar and vanilla. It definitely improves with age and I would recommend making at least one day, if not two days in advance for optimal flavor.

Fantastic! Made this to take to a chocolate themed Ladies Night. Served with Nilla Wafers, Ginger Snaps and Animal Crackers. Animal Crackers were the best! Definitely make this a day ahead. Tasted more like cheesecake than cookie dough so I added 2 tbsp extra brown sugar. After refrigerating overnight it absolutely tasted like cookie dough. Delicious!

After reading all the reviews I ended up adding an additional 2 tablespoons of brown sugar and an additional 1 teaspoon of vanilla. I also decided to add a tsp. of salt as that is an ingredient added to most cookie doughs. I used "mini" semi sweet chocolate chips and that was definitely the perfect size chocolate chip for this dip. This was a huge hit at my party 3 days ago and I've had several ask for the recipe. I made it the day before the party and served it with mini "nilla" wafers, chocolate teddy grahams, and animal crackers. Thanks for such a great recipe!
Yes, add the extra brown sugar and then sandwich it between 2 vanilla wafers. Chill it overnight and then you'll have mini cookie dough cheesecakes!

I doubled the recipe, added 2 & 1/2 cups of semi-sweet chocolate chips, & served it with graham cracker cookies. Everyone at the Bears game loved it because it had the salt from the graham crackers & the sweet from the dip. Twelve people asked for the recipe!?????

This was good! We all felt that it didn't quite hit the 'cookie dough' notes for us, but it was a nice, fun dessert dip. I used mini chocolate chips and topped with a little colored sprinkles to make it extra pretty! We dipped butter cookies, apples and pretzels. I would probably male this again!

Did a bunch of dips for a gathering and needed something sweet and this worked great. I used graham cracker bears. They were a little small, so would look for bigger but not too big graham crackers since it is pretty sweet. I also added the sprinkles for the colors.

I made this as written and it flew off the plate at a picnic. Afterwards, I agreed that it was more cheese cake tasting, so in addition to doubling the brown sugar and vanilla, I added some peanut butter extract. Yummier that way.
Very good. I added a little extra vanilla and brown sugar along w a 1/2 cup of peanutbutter to disguise the cream cheese taste. I also used M&M's to add some color.

This is a really yummy dip! I agree, it is more "cheesecake-y" than cookie dough, but yummy none the less. I adjusted the recipe as other had commented, doubling the brown sugar and the vanilla. I also altered it the second time I made it and substituted peanut butter for the butter....it was awesome (and seemed a little more virtuous than using the butter!) Love this dip and have shared it with my friends.
So popular at Christmas, used chocolate and regular teddy grahams as scoops!
Did exactly as recipe and it was a big hit people even asked for the recipe
This should be called Chocolate chip cheesecake dip. If that's the taste you are looking for you will like it.

I loved it. I had a final project to do last year and my teacher loved it too. I would totally make it again. 

:D
People raved about this! Yummm!
I served with graham crackers and sliced apples and pears - huge hit.

It's too cheesecake tasting. I tried the other suggestions and still nothing like cookie dough. A friend told me peanut butter. 3/4 a cup will get it to the color and flavor of cookie dough. Peanut butter fixes everything!
This was a good dish. I added extra vanilla in it.

This is a fantastic dessert that is incredibly easy to make. I do add a pinch of salt, but only for the natural preservative effects. Other than that, I make no changes. The number of compliments I have received when I have made this are almost guilt-inducing since it is so quick and easy to make.
